### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3487ccc12a6ad00dc75450f3f8b29a8a0630701d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2c00f6f976a48079e0cbfcdfd3067e4df73f9e29` — the merge of head `c7abcc64bf8a78c513e3b10328eeb40f8dee41df` into base `3487ccc12a6ad00dc75450f3f8b29a8a0630701d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2c00f6f976a48079e0cbfcdfd3067e4df73f9e29 && git checkout 2c00f6f976a48079e0cbfcdfd3067e4df73f9e29
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3487ccc12a6ad00dc75450f3f8b29a8a0630701d c7abcc64bf8a78c513e3b10328eeb40f8dee41df && git checkout -B drift-repro 3487ccc12a6ad00dc75450f3f8b29a8a0630701d && git merge --no-ff c7abcc64bf8a78c513e3b10328eeb40f8dee41df

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3487ccc12a6ad00dc75450f3f8b29a8a0630701d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `d4f1efa3f039a5ba1a294549b42a0ed0ce033527`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #31792 (body; claim 6732012750; triage 6732618138; dev report 6733733052), the seat's ruling (c) on the dev's Step 0 (`31792-step0.md`), PR #31837's body and file list, the net diff `56cac5eb..d4f1efa3` (merge base with `main`; five files, +228 / -28, matching the report's line budget), and the check-runs on the head. Background only: delta review 6731976766 on PR #31751 and ruling 6691022506. Code outside the diff (`@objectstack/metadata-core` `package-closure.ts` and `customization-pair-lookup.ts`, the protocol's `ensureCustomizationPackage`, the objectql registry's `residualOwnerDependenciesOf`) was read to judge the diff, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Both branches of `newSimilarTargetRefusal` read `packageDependencyClosure(target, registry)`. RIGHT for ruling (c).** It is the save gate's closure: `resolveWritePackageScope` is the same call over `engine.registry`, and the runtime reads `ql.registry`, which is the same registry. It is computed once, after the not-installed and read-only refusals, so those two answers and their order are unchanged. The import comes from `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, which this file already imports (`isWritablePackage`), so no package edge is added. The three judges named in the card now give one answer for the same pair. The save gate still decides pair rows with `isPairOf`, and its scope is now the same as this rule's.
2. **The size of the widening. NOT EXACTLY the source's App pair and the App's members. The code is right under (c), but the declaration is wrong (must-fix ③.1).** I read `widenPairClosureToAppMembers` and `packageDependencyClosure` against the diff. Compared with the bare walk `resolvePackageClosure(target, getPackage)`, the new closure accepts three more groups:
   - (i) **An App pair also accepts its members' declared closures.** For each member M with `pairOf(M) = APP.custom`, the widening adds M and every package M declares, transitively. Example: a package X that a member depends on, but that the App does not declare and that is no member, now lands in an explicit `package: APP.custom` on both doors (`200` where it was `409 outside_closure`). APP.custom is not X's pair: `pairOf(X)` is X.custom, or X's own App's pair.
   - (ii) **A permission set's objects branch takes the same wider closure for any source.** An explicit `package: APP.custom` is now accepted for a set that grants on objects owned by any App member, or by a member's dependency. That includes a set authored in the environment, which has no source package and so asks no closure question.
   - (iii) **A non-pair target is not byte-for-byte the bare walk.** `packageDependencyClosure` reads through `closurePackageReader`. When a target declares a dependency on a recorded residual owner (ADR-0130 D4: a stack's top-level owner, with no package record), the walk now continues into that owner's declared dependencies. Before, it stopped there. Any writable target with such a dependency now accepts sources and objects in those dependencies, on both doors and in both branches.

   **No target outside the save gate's closure is accepted.** Every request newly accepted is one that the save into that target would itself accept. The arms that must stay unchanged do stay unchanged. A writable package that declares the App but not the member gets no widening, because `customizationBasePackageId` is null for a non-pair id. It stays `409 outside_closure`, and both new CONTROLs pin that. A legacy MEMBER.custom (`pairOf` of no package) is not widened. The pair of a standalone base pairs only the base. An installed pair that dropped its App dependency is not widened, and the judge-before-create pin covers it. Option (b)'s red line, "any writable target depending on the App", is not crossed. But the PR body says "a non-pair target's closure is byte-for-byte the bare walk", and the changeset says "every other explicit `package` is judged exactly as before". Both are false for (i) to (iii).
3. **The objects branch still refuses what it should. RIGHT.** It narrows against the same closure as the source branch, so it refuses an object outside the target's save-gate closure. The permission-set CONTROL (`SUITE_EXT`) still answers `409 outside_closure` with no ensure and no save. What it now accepts beyond the old answer is (ii) and (iii) above, both in the save gate's scope. When `objects` is absent or empty, the branch asks nothing, as before.
4. **Judge before ensure. RIGHT.** In `land`, the multi-replica probe from #31751 still runs first. After it, `pairOf(owner, installedManifestsOf(ql.registry))` is the same derivation the ensure uses (`installedManifestsOfEngine(this.engine)` over the same registry). When that pair is installed, the target rule judges it before `ensure.call`. The pin with the pair installed but lacking its App dependency answers `409 outside_closure`. The ensure is never called, and nothing is published, stored or registered, so the package list does not change. **When the pair is not yet installed**, the code cannot judge it before the ensure, because nothing is there to judge. The fix relies on a construction: the creating ensure writes the pair writable and declaring its App, `pairOf(owner)` is that pair, and so the widened closure holds `owner`. The real-registry 200 pins exercise that path (no pair; only the legacy pair; a standalone base). A refused default landing therefore creates no pair on a real registry. The remaining way to leave a pair behind is a save refused after the ensure. That path is documented and existed before; its answer is the save's, not this rule's sentence. Nit ③.5 covers the one composition where the construction does not hold.
5. **"Nothing was written" is now literally true. RIGHT.** On the explicit path, the target is judged before `land` and `registerFlow` is never called (CONTROL). On the default path, a pair that is already installed is refused before the ensure, and the pin shows the engine copy withdrawn and no row stored. On a real registry, the post-ensure judge cannot refuse a pair it has just created. The message text itself does not change, and its clause "declares no dependency on …" stays accurate for every target the rule can still refuse.
6. **Single node and multi-replica agree with #31751. RIGHT.** When the App pair is present, both topologies answer `200` into APP.custom and create nothing. This is #31751's pin, edited as a forced edit (③.3). It still asserts that the two answers are equal and that the package count does not change. When the pair is absent, multi-replica keeps #31751's `MULTI_REPLICA_PACKAGE_CHANGE_REFUSED`, raised before anything is created, and single node now creates the pair and lands with `200`. That is #31751's R3 split, unchanged. When the pair is installed but refused, the probe passes (the pair exists), the pre-judge answers `409` on both topologies, and nothing is created.
7. **The permission-set door's explicit `package: APP.custom` is now accepted. RIGHT.** A member's set that grants on a member-owned object `suite_lead`, sent with `package: APP.custom`, answers `200` and is saved there. The ensure runs once, for the earlier default landing only. Both branches now pass: the source branch through the widened closure, and the objects branch because `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure` keeps the member's object. The rig's registry is a test double, made faithful by the forced edit in ③.3. The same shared function is pinned on the real `ObjectQL` registry through the flow door. `permission-set-clone.ts` is unchanged, as ruled: its default landing never asks the closure rule.
8. **Public surface. No movement.** No export changes. `TargetRegistry` is module-private; it gains the optional `getAllPackages`. `automation.ts` adds `installedManifestsOf`, `pairOf` and `InstalledPackageSource` from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which runtime already depends on (#31751). There is no spec, schema or metadata-protocol change.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/31792-new-similar-app-pair-closure.md`:** `'@objectstack/runtime': patch`. Runtime is the only package with a source change. **RIGHT.**
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`:** no authorable key, value, type or meaning moves, so this is `patch` under ruling A on #25105, where the level follows this line alone. **RIGHT.**
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`.** I read it against `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` in the changeset body and in the PR body. In both, the key starts the line and the token `yes` is the first thing after the colon. The arm is `(widening)`, with no alternation. The trailing `— widened: …` is reasoning, which the reader accepts and does not read. It reads as `declared · yes · widening` and matches the claim. The value and the arm are **RIGHT**: a request that was refused is now accepted, and nothing is narrowed. The pins agree: every CONTROL is green on base and on head, and the pre-existing outside-closure refusals still answer as before. **The enumerated reasoning under-states the accept-set (①.2, must-fix ③.1).** `Check Changeset`: success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **MUST-FIX: the declaration does not cover the whole widening.** The changeset's `Clause-②:` reasoning, the changeset prose ("A target that is not the source's pair keeps its own declared dependencies, so every other explicit `package` is judged exactly as before") and the PR body ("adds only packages whose `pairOf` is that pair", "a non-pair target's closure is byte-for-byte the bare walk") all leave out ①.2 (i) to (iii), which the code accepts. This is the declaration face, and the line is the accept-set's record. The remedy is text only:
   - State the rule as "accepted when the source's package, and each object's owner, is in `packageDependencyClosure(target)`, the save gate's write scope".
   - Name the arms: an App pair accepts its members and their declared closures; a set's objects branch accepts objects owned there; a target's declared residual owner is walked through its declared dependencies.
   - Remove "exactly as before" and "byte-for-byte".
   - Apply the same correction to the two code comments that say the same thing: the header of `new-similar-target.ts` ("only the packages whose pair it is (`pairOf`)") and the `land` comment in `automation.ts` ("holds every package the pair pairs").
2. **ESCALATED to the seat: does ruling (c) cover ①.2 (i) to (iii)?** The ruling was given on Step 0's description: "widening applies only to a pair that declares its App, and only adds packages whose pairOf IS that pair". The implementation does exactly what (c) says, the save gate's own closure, so I read all three as inside the ruling. But the premise of the ruling under-stated them, and the seat should confirm. If the seat confirms, ③.1 is text only. If it does not, the fix is no longer (c).
3. **Forced edits. ACCEPTED; both are named and both are test-only.**
   - (1) #31751's pin "a member whose App's pair this replica already serves…" now asserts `200` into APP.custom on both topologies, with no package created. The card asked for this edit by name.
   - (2) The permission-set rig's fake ensure now declares the App, which the real door writes (ruling 6691022506), instead of the member. Its fake registry gains `getAllPackages`, which the widening reads. Its fixture gains `suite_lead` (owned by the member), `SUITE_LEAD_SET`, and `SUITE_EXT` (a writable package declaring only the App). These are the edits named in the seat's ruling. No other existing case changes in the diff.
4. **Dev deviations.**
   - Option (c) instead of (a) or (b): **ACCEPTED**, by the seat's ruling.
   - The Step 0 worktree reused under another path: **ACCEPTED**. It leaves no trace on the surface.
   - The live-server confirmation that triage asked for is **NOT MEASURED**: **ACCEPTED as recorded, and left to the seat.** The reach is the real `ObjectQL` and protocol rig. No example in the tree installs an App whose member ships a flow.
   - `open_questions: []`. No question is outstanding apart from ③.2.
5. **NIT.** The construction behind ①.4 needs a registry with `getAllPackages`, and so does the claim in `land`'s comment that "a pair the ensure creates is never refused below". A composition whose `ql.registry` has no `getAllPackages` falls back to the bare walk. There, an App member's default landing would again be refused after a creating ensure, with "Nothing was written". The real `ObjectQL` registry has the method, so this is not reachable in the shipped composition. A one-line note in that comment would be enough.
6. **SHOULD-FIX: pin the extra arm, or record that it is unpinned.** None of the 91 cases exercises ①.2 (i): an explicit APP.custom for a flow from a member's dependency that is neither the App nor a member. After the seat answers ③.2, add a pin for whichever answer the seat gives, positive or CONTROL, or name the arm as unpinned in the PR body.
7. **Gates (check-runs on `d4f1efa3`, read at 2026-11-09T06:29Z).**
   - **Success:** Check Changeset; Check PR Size; Governed Surface Queue Guard; PR-body guards; Lint · ESLint; Lint · PM dispatch-gates; Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests; Lint · scoped · query-options erasure; Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus; Type Check · source gates; Type Check · debt ledger; Dogfood Regression Gate; Test UI; Live E2E UI; Plan Test Core shards; Flag docs; Auto Label; filter.
   - **Still in progress:** Test Core (1/8 to 8/8); Build Core; Type Check · workspace; Type Check · consumer gates; Lint · docs & code guards; Lint · CI, release & engine gates; Lint · repo & tooling gates.
   - **Failed:** none so far.
   - **Skipped:** the remaining runs, which are opt-in, UI-scoped or matrix placeholders.
   - The verdict below does not cover the runs still in progress. Landing waits on them.
8. **Dev claims I noted but did not rely on:** the base leg (7 red, 84 green), the three ablations (6, 1 and 5 red) and the full suites. I read the pins. They assert ①.4 to ①.7, which are what those ablations would turn red.

The runtime behaviour is unchanged since `d4f1efa3` (①.1), so the prior record's derived judgments ①.1 and ①.3 to ①.8 stand as written. Its ① covered the accept-set, the objects branch, judging before the ensure, the "Nothing was written" text, the single-node and multi-replica answers, the permission-set door's explicit APP.custom, and the public surface.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Runtime code: no change beyond comments. CONFIRMED.**

2. **The declaration now matches that accept-set (prior ①.2, must-fix ③.1). FIXED, RIGHT.**
   - **Changeset.** The `Clause-②:` reasoning states the rule as membership in `packageDependencyClosure(target)`, the save's own write scope. The source's package, and each object's owner for a permission set, must be in it. It names the three cases:
     - (i) An App pair that declares its App also reaches the App's members and each member's declared dependencies, transitively.
     - (ii) The objects check reaches the objects those packages own.
     - (iii) A target that declares a residual owner (ADR-0130 D4) reaches that owner's declared dependencies.
     
     It adds that nothing outside that closure is accepted. "Unchanged" became "Still refused", and that sentence is true: a package declaring only the App, and any target whose save-gate closure lacks the source or an object's owner, still get 409.
   - **PR body.** The `Clause-②:` line carries the same rule and the same three cases. The maintainer summary (维护者速读) lists the same three additions. The `new-similar-target.ts` bullet says the rule is membership and points to (i) to (iii).
   - **`new-similar-target.ts` header.** It states the rule as membership and lists (i) to (iii). I checked each against `widenPairClosureToAppMembers` and `closurePackageReader` in `@objectstack/metadata-core`. The member walk adds each package whose `pairOf` is the pair, plus that package's own declared closure, minus the pair itself. The residual reader is consulted only for an id that has no package record.
   - **`resolveCloneTarget` docblock and the comment in `land`.** Both now say the rule is membership in the save gate's closure, which for a pair declaring its App holds the App's members, `owner` among them. That is true for a member, and for a package that is its own unit (its pair declares the package itself).
   - **The three false sentences are gone** from the changeset, the three code comments and the PR body:
     - "every other explicit `package` is judged exactly as before",
     - "byte-for-byte the bare walk",
     - "adds only packages whose `pairOf` is that pair".
     
     I grepped all four carriers. The only `byte-for-byte` and `exactly as before` matches left in `automation.ts` are at lines 1357, 3660 and 4121. All three predate this PR and are about other subjects.
3. **The new pin for case (i) (should-fix ③.6). FIXED, RIGHT.**

   - **Why it measures case (i).** That is case (i) exactly: geo is neither the App nor a member, and APP.custom is not geo's own pair (`pairOf(geo)` is `com.acme.geo.custom`). The pair reaches geo only through the member's declared closure.
   - The dev reports the pin red on base and red under the bare-walk ablation. Both are what the closure code read above implies.
   - It runs on the real `ObjectQL` registry.
   - Cases (ii) and (iii) remain without a dedicated pin. The seat's ruling asked for one pin, for (i), so they are not owed.

### ② Semver level

- **Unchanged and RIGHT.** The changeset is `patch` for `@objectstack/runtime`, with `Metadata-protocol: none` (ruling A on #25105).
- **The rewritten `Clause-②:` lines still read correctly.** I checked them in the changeset and in the PR body against `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`:

  - `yes` is the first token;
  - the arm is `(widening)`, with no alternation;

  It reads as declared · `yes` · `widening`. The seat's ruling 6733829954 keeps both the line and the level.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Prior must-fix ③.1: FIXED** (①.2).
2. **Prior escalation ③.2: ANSWERED** by the seat in ruling 6733829954. Option (c) includes cases (i) to (iii), and the rule is membership in the save gate's closure. The code and the text now agree with that ruling.

5. **Prior ③.3 and ③.4 (forced edits and deviations): stand as accepted.** Round 2 adds one deviation, on who patched the PR body. I **ACCEPT** it:

   - The case (i) pin red on base and under `ABLATED_31792`.
